title: Brakes keep working while a session waits on your answer
why: Your gripe, Oct 26: a local UI/UX session waited on your question while its background agents kept working; the Mac ran out of storage and they crashed. Once you answered, the session saw the brake at once.
note: Finding, Oct 26 (claude-settings main 54be9f1): the machine-load brake (c14) read memory and disk only on a lane-start call, so lanes already running were never braked, whatever the main session was doing. Built: PR 642 ("brake a running lane at a full machine", draft, head 46a9060). Each background agent's own shell command and file write reads the load inside the guard hook that already runs; at full it is refused and told to stop and report. The main session is never braked, so it can free space. Red on main, green on the branch; Sonnet review round 1 clear, its three notes fixed. Not built: a watcher (the mandate forbids a timer or long-lived process) and a 'pause while a question waits' rule (the brake no longer depends on the wait). Deferred: shiv's word on the per-write read, which bends outcomes-mechanize-rules and c14's 'no per-call reading'; recommended keep as built. Asked: waiting page item c77-brake-running. Mac proof not needed: background lanes' payloads carry agent_id, measured live Oct 26 (decision a-kill-by-pid-needs-an-owned-pid, liaison). Port: no, the guard installs from claude-settings into every repo already. Placed ahead of c75 (triage, Oct 26). Oct 26 (waiting page): your answer to the brake question was "none of these"; the waiting-page thread is rewriting the options. The no-hang question idea is c84.
ask: None: the Mac proof brief was dropped, because the measurement it asked for already exists (decision a-kill-by-pid-needs-an-owned-pid).
